content: Cryptococcal antigen screening is conditionally recommended for adolescents, but the evidence supporting this recommendation is of low quality. A negative Xpert® MTB/RIF test, particularly when performed on cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), or a negative LF-LAM test does not definitively rule out tuberculosis (TB). For co-trimoxazole prophylaxis, it is strongly recommended for adults, adolescents, and children with severe or advanced HIV clinical disease (WHO clinical stage 3 or 4) and/or a CD4 cell count below 350 cells/mm³, based on moderate-quality evidence. In areas with high prevalence of malaria and/or severe bacterial infections, co-trimoxazole prophylaxis should be initiated regardless of CD4 count or WHO stage, as a conditional recommendation supported by moderate-quality evidence. For children under five years of age, co-trimoxazole prophylaxis is prioritized regardless of CD4 count or clinical stage, with strong evidence supporting this approach. Discontinuation of co-trimoxazole prophylaxis is conditionally recommended for individuals who are clinically stable on antiretroviral therapy (ART), have evidence of immune recovery, and are virally suppressed, though the evidence for this is of low quality. TB preventive treatment is strongly recommended for individuals who do not report symptoms such as cough, fever, weight loss, or night sweats, as they are unlikely to have active TB. These individuals should be offered isoniazid preventive therapy (IPT) for at least six months, regardless of their degree of immunosuppression, ART status, prior TB treatment, or pregnancy status. In high TB incidence settings, adults with unknown or positive tuberculin skin test status, and in whom active TB has been ruled out, should receive at least 36 months of IPT. For children older than 12 months living in high TB prevalence settings, six months of IPT is recommended if they are unlikely to have TB disease based on symptom screening and have no contact with a TB case. For children younger than 12 months, IPT is recommended only if they have been in contact with a TB case and active TB has been ruled out. Children living with HIV who have completed TB treatment should receive an additional six months of IPT. Pre-emptive antifungal therapy with fluconazole (800 mg/day for two weeks, followed by 400 mg/day for eight weeks, and maintenance with 200 mg/day) is conditionally recommended for individuals with a positive blood cryptococcal antigen test and CD4 counts below 100 cells/mm³, provided lumbar puncture excludes cryptococcal meningitis or is not feasible. This recommendation is based on low-quality evidence. If viral load monitoring is available, antifungal therapy can be discontinued when the CD4 count is at least 100 cells/mm³, with suppressed viral load, based on conditional recommendations and low-quality evidence. The guideline development process adhered to WHO policies, including declarations of interest and conflict management. The GRADE methodology was used to assess the quality of evidence and the strength of recommendations. Strong recommendations reflect confidence that the benefits outweigh the risks, while conditional recommendations indicate uncertainty or applicability to specific groups or settings.
